message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | Key Points | |------|------------------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after you move out (unless you and the landlord agree otherwise).
• Landlord may keep up to one month’s rent for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Landlord must provide an itemized list of deductions.
• If you disagree, you can file a claim in small‑claims court. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity). | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, you can withhold rent *only* if the issue is serious and the landlord has been notified in writing. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of a month‑to‑month lease: 30‑day written notice.
• For a fixed‑term lease: notice must be given before the lease expires. | • Written notice is required; oral notice is not sufficient. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violation).
• If you don’t comply, the landlord can file an unlawful detainer action. | • You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | • For a fixed‑term lease, rent can only change at the end of the term unless both parties agree. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | • “Emergency” includes fire, flood, gas leak, etc. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | • This is enforced under the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal law. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem after notice, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent *only* if the landlord is in default. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Lease Terms** | • All lease terms must be in writing and signed by both parties. | • Oral agreements are enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • Even if you sign a month‑to‑month agreement, you can request a written lease for clarity. | • A written lease protects both parties. | --- #### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** - Keep copies of all communications (emails, texts, letters). - Take photos or videos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Give Written Notice** - Use certified mail or a delivery service that provides proof of receipt. 3. **Know When to Withhold Rent** - Only do so after giving written notice and waiting for the landlord to respond. - Consider consulting an attorney or a tenant‑rights organization first. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** - **Texas Tenants Union** – offers free legal advice and resources. - **Legal Aid of North Texas** – provides representation for low‑income tenants. - **Local bar associations** often have lawyer referral services. 5. **File a Complaint** - If the landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or the local housing authority. --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Have you received a written lease? - [ ] Are you aware of the required notice periods? - [ ] Do you know how to properly document maintenance requests? - [ ] Have you kept records of all rent payments? - [ ] Do you know where to seek help if you face eviction or discrimination? --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, timely return of your security deposit, privacy, and protection against unfair eviction or discrimination. If you encounter problems, document everything, give proper notice, and consider seeking legal help if necessary.
